title: Powers
summary: Choose a power set around the role you want to play.

sections.title: How powers work
items: Choose your power set during character creation. Active powers unlock as you level; all active powers in your set are available at level 30.
Every power set supports the Damage role. Each also has a support role: Tank, Controller, or Healer.

sections.title: Tank power sets
items: Fire, Ice, Earth, Rage, and Atomic support tanking. Tanks attract enemy attention and absorb attacks to protect the group.

sections.title: Controller power sets
items: Gadgets, Mental, Light, Quantum, and Munitions support controlling. Controllers supply group power and incapacitate enemies.

sections.title: Healer power sets
items: Sorcery, Nature, Electricity, Celestial, and Water support healing. Healers restore the health of their teammates.

sections.title: Starting choices
items: Fire, Gadgets, Ice, Mental, Nature, and Sorcery are the classic character-creation power sets. Check current in-game access before purchasing additional powers.

sections.title: Roles, stats and additional powers
items: Tanks emphasize Defense, Health and Dominance, draw enemy attention, absorb attacks and provide group immunity to control effects.
Controllers emphasize Vitalization and Dominance, restore group Power and incapacitate enemies. Healers emphasize Restoration and Power to restore group Health.
All power sets can play Damage, emphasizing Precision and Might to defeat enemies and complete objectives.
Spend stat points in the movement-mode tree or Iconic Powers to gain additional active abilities.

sections.title: Complexity
items: Character Creation, as of 2025, classifies Powers by their complexity to use:
Simple: Fire, Munitions, Electricity
Standard: Sorcery, Mental, Ice, Quantum
High: Gadgets, Nature, Earth, Light, Water
Very High: Celestial, Rage, Atomic

sections.title: Atomic
items: Utilize the power of nuclear energy, rearranging the atomic structure of yourself, your allies, and your enemies at will. Split Atoms, cause Thermochemical Explosions, and burn under the intense Nuclear Pressure causing unreal destruction. Transmute into fortified metal and reorganize your atomic structure to protect you and your allies or harness the power of the building blocks of all matter to lay waste to your enemies. Explode with harmful radiation, reducing your enemies to ash and speeding up your recovery. Manipulate the subatomic structure of enemies to shield you and your allies.

sections.title: Celestial
items:
Keep your allies alive with cleansing Holy Magic or Dark Unholy rituals. Characters using Celestial Powers can shape the forces of the universe, Bless their allies and/or Curse their enemies. Wield divine powers to restrain and overwhelm your enemies and to soothe the wounds of your allies.
Command dark powers to restrain and overwhelm your enemies and to mend the wounds of your allies.

sections.title: Earth
items: Characters that choose earth will rumble on to the scene and shake things up. Earth Powers can be used for both Tanking and Damage and features a Tanking mechanic that defers damage to a player's summoned Golem. Shape Earthen constructs to crush enemies and reinforce allies. Call mighty, Earth-shaking forces to rattle and daze opponents.

sections.title: Electricity
items: Characters that choose electricity will imbue themselves with lightning. Electricity characters use these powers to shock their enemies or revitalize allies. They also want to spread their electricity so they can do as much damage to groups as possible. Electrify your enemies and resuscitate your allies. Manipulate and damage enemies with electrostatic forces.

sections.title: Fire
items:
Players who choose to wield the wild and unpredictable forces of fire have to be tough. Fire characters like to get up front and blast away at enemies, and therefore they tend to draw a lot of attention. Cause flames to well up around your character, causing damage to anyone in the vicinity.
Flames burst forth, searing your opponents and their nearby allies.

sections.title: Gadgets
items: Characters with the gadget power will find themselves pulling out all manner of devices from their pockets and pouches. On the front lines, a well-placed gadget will help you control not only the enemy but the battlefield itself. Gadget characters are crafty and use their heads to place their devices strategically to achieve victory. Slip through the shadows and deploy cunning gadgets to manipulate the battlefield. Employ a variety of devious and deadly contraptions to baffle your foes.

sections.title: Ice
items: Characters that choose to master subzero temperatures make for challenging foes. During combat, ice wielders have the ability to lock down opponents who come within their chilling reach. Ice forms around you and enemy attacks don't seem to land. By using your powers to create defenses for yourself, you are a master of mitigating damage. When the occasional attack does strike true, the cold is passed on to your attacker, often freezing them in their tracks. Icy winds dance at your command, allowing you to push and pull enemies around the battlefield. No one can escape your arctic blasts, which allows you to control the direction of the fight.

sections.title: Light
items: The rings that grant the ability to create Hard Light Constructs are given to only a chosen few. In times of great crisis, however, the Green Lantern and Sinestro Corps may choose individuals to be reservists, thereby swelling the ranks of Light Powered heroes and villains. Those who wield the power of Light are ideal front-line combatants dealing massive damage with imaginative constructs, or supporting their allies when the fight gets thickest. Heroes wield the green power of Will, while Villains use the yellow power of Fear. Light characters can chain deadly and devastating combinations called Construct Combos by using a power followed by certain weapon combos. A Light powered warrior is tough to defeat when charging in to battle with deadly constructs. Rain devastation on your enemies with missiles and bombs, blast them with a hail of bullets, or smash them out of the way with brute force. In the midst of a tough group battle the power of Light can be used to support the team in many ways. Throttle and stun an enemy with a giant hand or use a blast of light to recharge your team's power.

sections.title: Mental
items: Characters with the mental superpower are masters of mind over matter. Using their unique abilities, they can move objects with a thought to defend themselves or damage an enemy. They can also use the force of their will in more subtle ways, such as creating illusions to disorient and confuse. Mental characters love to be where the action is and control the battlefield with their minds. With the brute force of your will, you can create force fields that encase enemies or send them flying down the street. By using your mental powers, create opportunities for surprise attacks. Such power can even make an opponent think they see something that isn't there.

sections.title: Munitions
items:
Lock, load, and become a master of explosives and ballistics. Run and gun as you cut paths of destruction through your enemies with big guns and bigger explosions. Use your ordnance expertise to take control on the battlefield or simply blast right through the fray. Lay waste to the battlefield and any enemies that happen to be there with military-grade ordnance.
Knowledge of up-and-coming prototype artillery is half of the battle.

sections.title: Nature
items:
Characters that choose the nature power will find themselves masters over primal forces. Nature characters draw upon these forces to keep their allies alive or wither their enemies away. When the battle gets really tough, they can also let the call of the wild surge through them and actually become a beast full of rage, cunning and animal instincts. Wield poisonous botanical powers to restrain and overwhelm your enemies and to soothe the wounds of allies.
Call forth the attributes of a variety of frightening and fantastic animals to dominate enemies and aid allies.

sections.title: Quantum
items: Manipulate time, control gravity and twist the very fabric of space itself! Characters using Quantum Powers can slow down opponents, change their density, or even teleport behind them by altering time, manipulating gravity, and folding space. Control the flow of time and control your enemies futures. Bring your enemies to their knees by manipulating space and generating graviton fields.

sections.title: Rage
items: Tap into the Rage of the emotional spectrum to create energy blasts, deadly blood plasma attacks, and even vicious constructs. Wield this Red Light with righteous fury or be driven by vengeance and petty anger. Anger powers allow you to eradicate your enemies through blind rage. Defer incoming damage and share your rage with your allies.

sections.title: Sorcery
items:
Characters who wield the unseen forces of the universe hold the power of life and death in their hands. Sorcerers can doom enemies to failure or ensure their allies have the power to carry on the fight. They are ideal for combat support, often tipping the balance of a fight with their spells.
Drawn to your mystical power, fantastic arcane creatures never leave your side. Choose wisely which pet you summon, for each will behave according to the mystic forces that created it. Whether attacking, defending, or performing some other fantastic feat, legions of powerful minions are at your service. The fate of many rests in your hands as you change the course of battle. Generate good or bad karma for you, your allies, or foes. Gathering these positive and negative energies allows you to elevate or enfeeble those around you.

sections.title: Water
items: Keep your allies alive with powerful storms and flowing water. Command water in and around allies and enemies. Bend and blast water into incredible streams and torrents to unleash a flood of destruction, or shape it into awe-inspiring constructs to wash away your enemies. Soothe the wounds of your allies or envelop them and yourself with the shielding power of water. And turn the tides of conflicts by pulling strength from the mystical energies of the ocean depths.

sections.title: Iconic Powers
items: Iconic Powers are special powers, which are uniquely associated with specific DC Universe characters. Examples of iconic powers are Heat Vision, Word of Power, and Neo-Venom Boost, which are associated with Superman, Shazam, and Bane, respectively. All characters can purchase iconic powers, regardless of the power set they chose at character creation.

sections.title: Artifact Powers
items: Certain artifacts grant access to new powers. Examples of such artifacts are The Omega Totality, M.E.R.C.Y. Amazotron Matrix, B.O.P. Commlink, Brand of Hecate and Source Shard. Artifact powers become available once the artifact is at least rank 80.

sections.title: Notes
items: All powers activated from the power tray and their combos cause damage based on Might.
Most powers support Power Interactions.
Character's main power set will affect the color as well as some other visual effects of weapon attacks. One of the most noticeable examples is Martial Arts' Spinning Punch combo.
Certain Allies and Artifacts can modify effects of powers.
Certain powers can be cast faster than their animation by use of Clipping.
Certain powers can be canceled early, for example finishers by pressing the jump button.
On March 31st, 2015, previous DLC packs were separated into Episodes, Powers, Upgrades and Legends characters.

Before game update 73 Power points could be reset and altered in-game through the use of the R.A.D. Kiosk, located in the Aquacultural area of the JLA Watchtower, or the B.A.D. Kiosk located in The Pit of the Hall of Doom. Now these devices are only used to reset skill points.

summary: Follow the green markers to complete investigation sets.

items: Investigation tokens use a green exclamation mark. They are a different collectible type from Collections and Player Briefings.

sections.title: Completion rewards

sections.title: Where to begin
items: The source organizes investigations into Gotham, Metropolis, and Global groups. Start with the linked Viva la Lucha Libre guide for Cape Carmine node locations; the remaining individual investigation guides still await review.

items: Investigations are a collectible similar to Player Briefings or Collections. Their tokens are marked with a green exclamation mark (!). Completing an investigation rewards the player with a piece of armor or an accessory that is of average level for the quests in the area.

title: Grab and Smash
summary: Retrieve five pieces of information inside the Cape Carmine Lighthouse duo.

sections.title: Before entering
items: The source identifies Arcane Edict #020 as the hero unlock. Its villain edict number is unspecified.
Track the mission in your Journal before queuing for Cape Carmine Lighthouse through On Duty. The source warns that the walk-in version does not work.

sections.title: Terminal route
items: After the Venom Supplier Diego fight, go through the door and look to the left.
Look in the room where you fight Killer Croc or Huntress.
Check the lobby for the Killer Croc and Deathstroke, or Huntress and Nightwing, fight.
Check the western side of the corridor leading to Bane.
Find the final terminal in the corridor leading to the exit.

sections.title: Rewards
items: The source lists 1,162 cash and a Source Mark. These values have not been verified in the current game.

sections.title: Mission objective and terminal views
items: Bane's street soldiers are trading information about increased magical activity in Gotham. Retrieve five pieces of information before the gang can profit from it.

Interact with all five terminals during the queued duo. If a terminal is not interactive, confirm this mission was tracked in the Journal before starting the run. The pictures below correspond to the five numbered map screenshots in Location & maps.

title: Cape Carmine Lighthouse
summary: Find the Gotham landmark, mission entrance, and duo setting.

sections.title: Which version are you entering?
items: The source describes a Gotham landmark, a level 9 mission instance, and a Tier 1 duo under this name. Check which version your objective requires.
The source lists level 30 access and two Source Marks for the duo. These requirements and rewards have not been checked in the current game.

sections.title: Inside the lighthouse
items: Bane and his Venom-powered gang occupy the lighthouse. Nightwing and Killer Croc pursue Bane and his Venom supply.
The encounter cast varies by faction and mode. The source identifies Deathstroke with the hero duo and Huntress with the villain duo.

sections.title: Related objectives
items: Grab and Smash requires the queued duo rather than the walk-in instance. Track that quest before entering.
The Viva la Lucha Libre investigation includes two parts inside the lighthouse. Use its individual landmark descriptions to locate those nodes.

sections.title: Inhabitants and faction encounters
items: Outside: Retaliators, Lieutenants, Hoppers and Razors; the Lighthouse Keeper, GCPD Rookies, Officer O'Brien and Fast Eddie.
Inside: Lieutenants, Muscle, Razors, Envenomed Guard Dogs, Retaliators, Strongmen and Bane.
The source lists Killer Croc for the villain solo and both duo factions; Nightwing for the hero solo and both duo factions. Deathstroke is specific to the hero duo and Huntress to the villain duo.

sections.title: Local objectives and history
items: The Lighthouse Keeper asks players to destroy 15 Venom Canisters. Several exobit spawn locations lie close together around the lighthouse.
The duo was introduced in Game Update 1 on February 14, 2011. Cape Carmine is named for comics artist Carmine Infantino.

title: Viva la Lucha Libre
summary: Locate six investigation parts around Cape Carmine and its instances.

sections.title: Route overview
items: This six-part investigation is spread across Cape Carmine in Gotham's East End, including the Distribution Center and Cape Carmine Lighthouse instances.
Several outdoor parts have alternate nodes. The location descriptions below preserve those alternatives rather than implying a single fixed spawn.

sections.title: Six investigation parts
items: Use the map references with the landmarks in this table. The source does not supply numeric coordinates for these nodes.

table.caption: Source-reported investigation locations
rows: Four possible nodes: sidewalks west of the western cargo ship or east of the eastern cargo ship at Gotham Docks.

Three possible nodes: northeast corner of the Old Soder Cola Plant block near the Distribution Center entrance; northwest corner of the block north of the plant; Stagg Stop gas station northeast of the plant.
Distribution Center: southern side room next to the room containing Venom Supplier Diego.
Sidewalk north of Cape Carmine Lighthouse, or stairs south of the lighthouse.
Cape Carmine Lighthouse: middle of the room where Nightwing or Killer Croc fights Bane's Streetgang.
Cape Carmine Lighthouse: southeast corner of the Bane fight room.

sections.title: Completion reward
items: The source lists Gangster's Jacket, using the Classic Biker style, as the completion reward.
Heroes receive completion mail from Harvey Bullock; villains receive it from the Penguin. Read the message at a mail terminal.

sections.title: Investigation node views
items: Match these six scene images to the numbered map screenshots and location table. Outdoor nodes can have alternate positions; collect only one copy of each named part.

sections.title: Recordings and reward mail

Hero completion mail is from Harvey Bullock, subject Pounding the Mat; villain mail is from the Penguin, subject A Bird in the Hand. Both attach Gangster's Jacket.

title: Out in the Streets
summary: Disrupt Bane's Venom shipments at the Cape Carmine docks.

sections.title: Objectives
items: Travel to Cape Carmine in Gotham. Defeat 15 Bane thugs protecting the Venom shipments.
Collect samples from 20 shipment crates, and stop 10 Strongmen carrying Venom crates before delivery.

sections.title: Finding the mission area
items: The investigation guide identifies the Gotham Docks at Cape Carmine as this mission's area. Its first investigation-part map shows the surrounding dock area, not every mission objective.

The same investigation guide places alternate first-part nodes on sidewalks west of the western cargo ship and east of the eastern cargo ship. These are investigation landmarks, not guaranteed quest target positions.

sections.title: Before moving on
items: Follow the tracked mission objectives for remaining crate and enemy targets. No exact target coordinates are supplied by the reviewed sources.
The linked hero playthrough explicitly names this quest; the next chapter covers House of Venom.

sections.title: Story context and results
items: Batman reports Bane's return to Gotham and warns that his gang is distributing Venom throughout the East End. Take shipment samples for analysis while disrupting the distribution operation.
After analysis, Oracle identifies the samples as a weaker version of Bane's usual Venom and warns that the steroid can damage the body.

title: House of Venom
summary: Locate Bane's distribution hub and take down Venom Supplier Diego.

sections.title: Objectives
items: Search for Bane's Venom Distribution Hub, interrogate his Street Soldiers, and confiscate Venom from his Razors.
Take down Venom Supplier Diego and arrest him. The mission source identifies him as the boss.

sections.title: Finding the hub
items: The mission article identifies the hub as the Distribution Center. The associated investigation guide places its entrance near the northeast corner of the Old Soder Cola Plant block in Cape Carmine.

An investigation node is also located in the southern side room next to Diego's room. The linked investigation maps provide entrance-area and interior context, not a marked route through every quest objective.

sections.title: Opposition and allies
items: The source lists Bane's minions, Muscle, Strongman, Razor, and Venom-affected dogs among the opponents.
The allies list distinguishes Nightwing for heroes and Killer Croc for villains. The linked video is a Batman-mentor hero playthrough.

sections.title: Gang war and supporting combatants
items: The Joker-backed Falcone crime family and Bane's Venom-charged gang are fighting over Gotham's East End. Investigate the supplier to stop the new Venom distribution.
The source also lists Falcone Family Hoods and Bane among the opposition, and Gotham Police among the allies. Oracle connects the mission to Bane's earlier attack that broke Batman's back.

title: Feats
summary: Earn feat points, gain skill points, and understand optional unlocks for alternate characters.

sections.title: Earning skill points
items: Feats reward completion of challenges across exploration, solo content, group instances, PvP, and other activities. Every 100 feat points grants one additional skill point, allowing progression beyond the points gained through leveling.

sections.title: Star ratings and points
items: Read the requirement of each feat before attempting it. Four-star feats are special rewards and do not necessarily demand more effort than three-star challenges.

sections.title: Unlocking feats on another character
items: Replay badges can grant eligible feats already earned by another character. This is optional: feats can still be earned by completing their normal requirements. Only feats shared by the characters are eligible, so movement-specific feats cannot be transferred to an incompatible movement type.

The source lists badge costs of 1, 3, 5, and 7 for feats worth 10, 25, 50, and 100 points respectively. Check the in-game unlock confirmation before spending badges. Some event-progression feats can instead be obtained on other characters by reclaiming their associated rewards.

sections.title: Finding your next goal
items: Use the feats menu to inspect requirements and progress. A yellow ribbon marks feats that also award a title. The menu was reorganized in Game Update 135; older screenshots and navigation instructions may differ from the current interface.

sections.title: Source overview
items: Feats Icon
One of the many features in DC Universe Online is the Feats section. Feats are self-contained challenges that award points upon completion.
Challenge Dynamo

DC Universe Online feats contain challenges covering every aspect of gameplay, including Exploration, Alerts, Raids and PvP. More feats will be added as new content becomes available in game, so additional feats can be expected on a regular basis.

sections.title: Feats Menu
items: The feats menu can be accessed by pressing the escape key, then clicking on the trophy icon at the bottom of the screen. This will bring up a list of options, the first option is feats.
Feats Menu
The feats menu is split into 3 sections: Categories, Recent Accomplishments and Progress Overview.
Categories section shows a list of subcategories for feats e.g. Exploration, Alerts, Solo Content and PVP.
Recent Accomplishments section shows the last 3 feats you completed.
Progress Overview section shows the total number of feats available in each subcategory and how many you have completed.
Feat providing a Title
Feats which grant titles are denoted by a yellow ribbon in the feats menu.
The game's original feats menu was completely reorganized with game update 135.

sections.title: Rewards
items: For every 100 points achieved the player will receive an additional skill point for their character. Completing feats will allow you to gain new skill points beyond what you can achieve through leveling alone.
The number of points awarded for completing each feat varies based on difficulty, easy feats award 10 points whereas the most difficult/time consuming award 50 points.

sections.title: Difficulty Rating/Points Awarded
items: Each feat has a star rating, which reflects the difficulty of accomplishing that feat. The star rating also indicates how many points you receive upon completion.
4 Star feats are generally not "hard to achieve" per se - there are plenty of 3 Star feats vastly more challenging or grindy - but most recently seemingly exclusive to limited-time special events.

sections.title: Difficulty Rating/Points Awarded - table 1
items: Source-listed entries. Follow the source references above for unconverted detail pages.

sections.title: Manual Feats Unlock
items: Manual feats unlock
Since game update 34 feats the player has achieved with another character can be unlocked with replay badges.
Unlockable feats will have a small green button in the overviews of the feat menu.
Feats can only be unlocked if they are shared between characters. E.g. an acrobat cannot unlock super-speed related feats and vice versa.

sections.title: Manual Feats Unlock - table 1
items: Source-listed entries. Follow the source references above for unconverted detail pages.

sections.title: Notes
items: 1 skill point is achieved every 100 feat points, thus you need to spend 100-120 replay badges to level up a character 10 skill points and 1000-1200 replay badges to level up a character 100 skill points .

Its not necessary to use replay badges, instead they are a way to speed up skill point progression by effectively buying feats that you've already obtained on another character. However, those feats you could buy with replay badges are still obtainable as normal. Some new players might assume that you must unlock the feats obtained with another character before you can obtain them on another, this is a misconception brought about by the term "unlock". Unlocking merely grants you the feat without going about the normal means of obtaining it.

More recent 100 points feats, achieved via the event progression system, can be achieved on other player characters by reclaiming their related rewards and thus don't need to be unlocked with replay badges.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Game update 135 completely restructured the original feats tree. Also, episode feats are now ordered by context, e.g. raid related feats, augment related feats etc.

sections.title: Difficulty estimates and completion plans
items: Browse the searchable Feats catalog for individual requirements, reward points and completion plans. Difficulty uses five bars: Simple, Routine, Demanding, Hard and Extreme. These are editorial estimates based on mechanics, coordination and time investment; they are independent of the game's feat-point stars.

Completion plans retain the exact source requirement and add conservative planning advice. Gear, group skill, availability and luck can change the effort. Read linked mission and item pages for detailed mechanics, and verify current requirements in the in-game Feats menu.

title: Equipment
summary: Understand weapons, costume pieces, and the other items your character carries.

sections.title: Choosing weapons
items: Your weapon type determines the attacks and combos available in combat. Weapon types offer different combinations of ranged and melee attacks. Characters can develop more than one weapon type; choose based on the attacks you want to use and your combat role.

sections.title: Costume equipment
items: Costume pieces contribute character statistics. Role and character-level requirements can restrict which pieces you can equip. Compare usable equipment separately from its visual style when choosing upgrades.

sections.title: Other item types
items: Inventory items serve several purposes beyond equipped armor and weapons. Trinkets and consumables can assist in combat, collection items contribute to sets, and base items provide decoration. Currency and crafting materials have separate progression uses.

sections.title: Weapon types
items: The source lists Bow, Brawling, Dual Pistols, Dual Wield, Hand Blaster, Martial Arts, One-Handed, Rifle, Shield, Staff, and Two-Handed. For cross-weapon combos, see the Weapon Mastery guide. Check current in-game access requirements for restricted weapon types.

sections.title: Source overview
items: Equipment is a term used to describe any and all items that can be equipped or used by Player Character while playing DC Universe Online.

sections.title: Items
items: Main article: Items
Items are miscellaneous objects that Player Characters can carry with them for varying purposes such as monetary gain, combat assistance, collection or decoration.
Other types of Items include:

sections.title: Weapons
items: Main article: Weapons
Weapons can be equipped by Player Characters to increase their combat strength.

A character's combat abilities and effectiveness in battle are defined by what weapon they use; some weapons specialize in ranged attacks, some in melee, and some dabble in both. In addition, while a Player Character is effectively free to choose to utilize any, and potentially all, weapon types, some weapons are suited better to some Combat Roles than others.

sections.title: Costumes
items: Main article: Costumes
Costumes provide additional points to the Player Character's statistics to make them more effective in combat.

Costumes can be divided based on Stylistic Appearance and/or Roles; a player's Role can determine whether or not they can use a certain Costume piece. Furthermore, a Player Character's Experience Level dictates whether a character is worthy of wearing/using a certain piece of Costume.

title: Weapon Mastery
summary: Unlock stronger weapon combos and chain attacks into another weapon type.

sections.title: Unlocking mastery
items: Weapon Mastery becomes available after spending the required stat points in a weapon tree. Unlocking mastery for your equipped weapon increases damage from its weapon combos. Check the tree in game for the exact point requirements.

sections.title: Multiple Mastery
items: Cross-weapon combos require the corresponding mastery unlocks in the other weapon trees. You do not need to own a secondary weapon item to perform its unlocked mastery combo. Unlocking the combo also adds an appearance option in the Style UI.

sections.title: Combo reference
items: Each row lists the secondary weapon trees and the four combo sequences recorded by the source. The first two sequences are labeled melee and the last two ranged in that reference. These are source-listed sequences, not independently tested damage rankings.

sections.title: Practice and appearance
items: The source notes that mastery combos can be performed without hitting an enemy or sparring target. Secondary and tertiary weapon appearances can be selected in the style menu, including a default energy-construct appearance using the primary character color.

sections.title: Source overview
items: Original WM Animation
Weapon Mastery is a system available to all players. It was introduced with the Amazon Fury Part I episode.

sections.title: Overview
items: Weapon Mastery requires a specific number of Stat Points spent in a Weapon Tree to unlock. The player gains increased damage when using weapon combos if Weapon Mastery is unlocked for the equipped weapon type.
Multiple Mastery allows combos into other Weapons if Weapon Mastery is unlocked in other Weapon trees.
Unlocking a Multiple Mastery combo will also add an appearance option for that weapon in the Style UI.
While you need the type and the mastery unlocked, you do not need to own the secondary weapon in order to complete the mastery combo.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Previously, in order to successfully exercise Weapon Mastery, the player needed to focus on an enemy or a Sparring Target. This has since been changed and you can perform the combos without hitting anything.

It is possible to set the weapon styles for the secondary and tertiary weapon via the style menu. There is a unique "Default" style for secondary and tertiary weapons that looks like a simple energy construct in the player's primary colour.

Neither Staff nor Shield appear in any other weapon tree's Mastery list. While Shield's exclusion is understandable due to being a fighting style only available with a purchase, Staff's exclusion is odd and unexplained. These are how many times a weapon type appears in other weapon trees:; 4: Dual Pistol; 3: Martial Arts, Hand Blaster, Bow; 2: Two Handed, Dual Wield, Brawling, One Handed; 1: Rifle

title: Artifacts
summary: Equip long-term upgrades and improve them with Nth Metal and catalyst breakthroughs.

sections.title: Equipping artifacts
items: Artifacts use dedicated equipment slots. Each artifact type can be equipped only once, so duplicate copies cannot fill multiple slots. Unlike frequently replaced combat-rating gear, artifacts develop through a longer-term investment in ranks.

sections.title: Obtaining your first artifact
items: The source describes an introductory Artifacts mission from John Constantine, available at level 20. After completing it, additional artifacts can be obtained from Constantine in the House of Legends, Watchtower, or Hall of Doom. Individual artifacts may also come from mission rewards, Time Capsules, or grants. Check the vendor and the specific artifact source before spending currency.

sections.title: Fortifying and breakthroughs
items: Use Nth Metal to add item experience through the artifact fortification interface. Higher-quality Nth Metal provides more experience. Gaining enough experience increases the artifact rank and its statistical bonuses.

Every 20 ranks is a milestone requiring specific catalysts for a breakthrough. The source identifies John Constantine and certain episode vendors as catalyst sources. Inspect the breakthrough requirements for your current artifact rather than assuming every milestone uses the same catalyst combination.

sections.title: Choosing an artifact
items: Artifacts can provide passive or active abilities as well as statistics. Match those effects to the role and play style you want to support. The available effects depend on the artifact and its rank; this overview does not supply unverified item-level statistics.

sections.title: Source consistency note
items: The source introduction still describes three artifact slots, while its update history records five slots from game update 155. The reproduced source overview below is historical in that respect; consult the current in-game inventory for slot availability.

sections.title: Source overview
items: An Artifact is a new type of gear equipped in three Artifact slots, and that you can rank up and fortify with Nth metal to unlock powerful bonuses. Unlike other types of gear that you replace frequently as you advance in combat rating, Artifacts require a long term investment and grow with your character. Many Artifacts will also grant new passive or active abilities starting from rank 80 to 200 in addition to stats, and will provide new options for how you build or play your character.
Each type of artifact can only be equipped once, it is not possible to equip two or three of the same artifact type at the same time.

sections.title: Obtaining Artifacts
items: You will get your first Artifact by completing the Artifacts Mission from John Constantine (available at level 20). Once completed, you can obtain additional Artifacts from Constantine in the House of Legends, Watchtower or Hall of Doom for 10 Source Marks.
Some artifacts are also available via mission rewards, Time Capsules, or the Grant system, although they are usually also available from Constantine for 10 Source Marks.

sections.title: Upgrading Artifacts
items: In your inventory, there is a new tab called Artifacts. Once you have an Artifact and some Nth Metal, you can combine the two to add Item Experience to the Artifact. Different kinds of Nth Metal are worth different amounts of Item Experience. Get enough Item Experience into your Artifact and it will increase in Rank. Each Rank gives a small, exponentially increasing stat boost. Every 20 Ranks is a Milestone Rank, which offers larger bonuses and requires specific Catalysts to breakthrough.

sections.title: Reagents
items: Nth Metal is the core reagent for your Artifact. Once you’ve acquired your first Artifact, you’ll be able to find Nth Metal as a rare drop from defeating NPCs. In addition, you’ll be able to get large caches of Nth Metal by completing the Vault and Stabilizer Fragmentation. Nth Metal comes in various qualities, with rarer, more refined pieces granting larger amounts of Item Experience when used to fortify your Artifact.
Sin Stones are another reagent for Artifacts. They are only available from Assassin Time Capsules.
Sunstones are yet another reagent for Artifacts. They are only available from Kryptonian Time Capsules.
Artifacts that players no longer wish to possess can be used as reagents to level up other artifacts. However less than half of the XP contained will be recycled.
Container Artifacts usually have their own special reagents.

sections.title: Catalysts
items: Catalysts are special items required to break through Milestone Ranks. These can be acquired from John Constantine and certain episode vendors. Each Milestone Rank requires a different and specific combination of Catalysts.

sections.title: Feats
items: Various feats are available related to artifacts.
Main article: General Feats

sections.title: Trivia
items: Artifacts will be temporarily disabled in PvP instances.
Artifacts were introduced with game update 76.
With hotfix 18/01/18 a second artifact slot was introduced making it possible to equip two different artifacts at the same time.
With hotfix 15/02/18 the maximum rank of artifacts was increased from 100 to 120.
With game update 84 the maximum rank of artifacts was increased from 120 to 160.
With game update 86 a third artifact slot was introduced making it possible to equip three different artifacts at the same time.
With game update 97 the maximum rank of artifacts was increased from 160 to 200.
With game update 155 a fourth and fifth artifact slot was introduced making it possible to equip five different artifacts at the same time.

Usually milestone rank 80 is at 39,920 experience, rank 100 at 82,499 experience, rank 120 at 167,659 experience, rank 140 at 337,979 experience, rank 160 at 678,722 experience, rank 180 at 1,178,722 experience and rank 200 is at 1,678,722 experience. The best freely available reagent yields 3,000 XP and is available as a bonus from Doctor Fate's Daily Rewards.

Game Update 171introduced the following changes to fortification:; To reduce clutter, the Fortify tab no longer displays max-rank artifacts or augments.; Selecting a large stack of reagents will now only insert into the preview as many items as are needed to reach the next Milestone Rank. You can still select the reagents a second time to use the entire stack if you want.

sections.title: Objectives
items: Travel to Cape Carmine in Gotham. Defeat 15 Bane thugs protecting the Venom shipments.
Contaminate 10 shipment crates. Stop 10 Strongmen carrying Venom crates before they finish their deliveries.

sections.title: Finding the mission area
items: The associated Viva la Lucha Libre investigation identifies the Cape Carmine dock area with this mission. Use its map for dock-area orientation, then follow the tracked mission markers for crates and enemies.
The map marks an investigation node, not all quest objectives. Target spawn coordinates are not provided by the reviewed sources.

sections.title: Story and next objective
items: The Joker wants Bane's operation driven off Falcone territory. Contaminate the supply rather than collect the samples required by the separate hero mission Out in the Streets.
The linked playthrough names this quest explicitly and continues toward the distribution-hub objectives in Poisoned Bait. Use the journal to confirm which objective is active.

title: Poisoned Bait
summary: Find Bane's Venom distribution hub and interrogate his street soldiers.

sections.title: Objectives
items: Search for Bane's Venom distribution hub. Find and interrogate 3 Bane Street Soldiers.
Defeat 10 of Bane's Razors and steal their Venom. Follow the active journal objective to distinguish these enemies from other gang members.

sections.title: Route and map
items: The associated investigation identifies its second-part area with Poisoned Bait and the hero's House of Venom mission. Use the plant/entrance-area map to reach this part of Cape Carmine.
The investigation marker is a landmark for the mission area, not a precise Street Soldier or Razor spawn. The source quest page does not supply individual target coordinates.

sections.title: Nearby freelance missions
items: Hood offers Mainliner. Circuitbreaker Tobias offers Intent to Sell. These are separate side missions listed by the source; track their own objectives if you accept them.

sections.title: Story context
items: The Joker sends you after Bane's main distributor. Interrogating the street soldiers advances the search; Calculator notes that the Falcones have hired Killer Croc, who already hates Bane.

title: Beatdown for Bane
summary: Enter Cape Carmine Lighthouse and help Killer Croc defeat Bane.

sections.title: Entrance and objective
items: Travel to Cape Carmine Lighthouse. The mission dialogue explicitly places the entrance up top, behind the light. Use the world map below to find the lighthouse, then the instance map for its interior.
Killer Croc is inside. Find Bane and defeat him to complete the main objective; Calculator then directs you back to the safehouse.

sections.title: Lighthouse Cleanup
items: The Lighthouse Keeper offers the separate Lighthouse Cleanup mission. The linked walkthrough shows its Venom-canister cleanup alongside the main route. Check the tracked objective before leaving the instance.

sections.title: Historical feat walkthrough
items: Jane Denton Gaming explicitly labels this run Beatdown for Bane. The description lists Lights Out in the Lighthouse at 1:54 and the Undefeated / School of Hard Knocks completion segment at 9:27.

The description associates Lights Out with clearing enemies and Venom canisters before Bane, Undefeated with avoiding a knockout, and School of Hard Knocks with defeating Bane without consumables or supercharge abilities. This is a 2015 recording; verify current feat requirements in the game before attempting them.

title: The Precipice of Fear
summary: Find all six of Dr. Crane's research notes around the East End and Gotham Sewer.

sections.title: Part 1: Fear Itself
items: On the top of a building under construction right in front of the East End Police Station, behind a Box Pallet.
Recording: Dr. Crane: " Experiment 905: Roosevelt said: 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself.' He was, of course, utterly wrong."

sections.title: Part 2: Anxiety's Sting
items: There are two nodes for this part. One is located just Southwest of the East End Bowery point in the map (behind the fence), while the other is two blocks West from the Bowery, under the railway to the North.
Recording: Dr. Crane: " Experiment 910: To acquaint the nervousness of a first date, with the sheer terror one must feel in a plane crash, does a disservice to us all."

sections.title: Part 3: Terror Suppression
items: South from Crime Alley, at the Malone Improvement District block. It's near a truck to the East.
Recording: Dr. Crane: " Experiment 504: The rostral anterior cingulate cortex gives us some semblance of control over our fear."

sections.title: Part 4: Hysteria's Song
items: There are two nodes for this part: one on the roof of the East End Free Clinic (image), and the other behind the Free Clinic.
Recording: Dr. Crane: " Experiment 79: Like Ichabod fleeing the Headless horseman, mediated thought is replaced with a stream of hysteria."

sections.title: Part 5: Pangs of Horror
items: Heroes will find this part inside the first room in the Gotham Sewer, in the dead-end tunnel to the South. A node for this part is also available for all players in the open-world zone, on the building Northwest from East End Free Clinic and South from the Amusement Mile area.
Recording: Dr. Crane: " Experiment 408: The Toxoplasma gondii parasite will actually suppress the rat's fear, making it actively seek out the scent-marked areas of cats."

images.label: Part 5: Pangs of Horror - location view

sections.title: Part 6: Phobia's Darkness
items: Heroes will find this part inside the final room in the Gotham Sewer, near the exit. A node for this part is also available for all players in the open-world zone, Northwest to Crime Alley, in the middle of the housing complexes.
Recording: Dr. Crane: " Experiment 81: Adverse reactions to specific stimuli can eventually be removed from the subject via carefully measured exposure."

sections.title: Reward and completion
items: Fear Gas Breather Helmet (Antifreeze head style). Heroes receive mail from Doctor Jeremiah Arkham thanking them for the research; villains receive mail from Doctor Jonathan Crane about recovering his early work.
Collect each of the six distinct parts. Alternate nodes described above are alternatives for the same part, not additional required collectibles.

title: Gorilla Bomb Components
summary: Find the six components of Grodd's devolution bombs around Little Bohemia.

sections.title: Part 1: Simian-Infused Payload Shell
items: Queensland Beach, in the vicinity of the mission Gorillas By The Sea
Recording: " Gorilla Technician Report: General Grodd brilliantly designed this to shred upon impact, ensuring maximum devastation!"

sections.title: Part 2: Chromosome 2 Diffuser Node
items: Southbank Commercial District, in the vicinity of the Devolving Citizen involved in the mission He Wants a Devolution, on the ground level across the street of a building with Metropolis University banners.
Recording: " Gorilla Technician Report: An ingenious device - it breaks down human genetic material for easy manipulation."

sections.title: Part 3: Simian-Infused Chassis
items: In front of the Queensland Boardwalk entrance, in the vicinity of the missions Gorilla Warfare and Boardwalk Assault
Recording: " Gorilla Technician Report: This chassis is infused with a metal alloy so advanced, the human's primitive weapons won't even leave a scratch."

sections.title: Part 4: Simium-231 Reactor Core
items: Southbank Commercial District, in the vicinity of the Devolution Units involved in the mission He Wants a Devolution, near Scout Tiken. The node is on the ground floor next to a fountain in front of a Cafe.
Recording: " Gorilla Technician Report: This Reactor Core can provide nearly endless power to any one of General Grodd's visionary devices."

sections.title: Part 5: Psionics-Sensitive Detonator
items: South of the Queensland Boardwalk, in the vicinity of the Neural Arrays involved in the mission He Wants a Devolution. Node is next to a Neural Arrays on the top of the commercial building comprised of Coffee shop with outdoor tables, Computers store, Books store, Video store, and a Billiards (you'll need to engage with Gorilla Technicians before collecting it).
Recording: " Gorilla Technician Report: General Grodd designed the detonator to pick up psychic vibrations so slight, even thinking about the sensor could trip the fuse. Uh oh."

sections.title: Part 6: Primary Reactor Rotor
items: Southbank Commercial District, in the vicinity of the Devolution Units involved in the mission He Wants a Devolution. The node is on the highest floating platform (players what don't have the flight movement style can use the teleporters on the lowest platforms to get there).
Recording: " Gorilla Technician Report: The Reactor is powerful enough to send devolution rays across the entire city!"

sections.title: Reward and completion
items: Bioshaped Gorillium Leggings. Heroes receive mail from the Flash saying STAR Labs will analyze the parts; villains receive a message from Grodd praising the power of gorilla technology.
Collect each of the six distinct parts. Alternate nodes described above are alternatives for the same part, not additional required collectibles.

title: Bane Brought Down
summary: Return to Batwoman at the East End Police Station after defeating Bane and choose a weapon reward.

sections.title: Turn-in and route
items: Speak to Batwoman inside the East End Police Station, also known as the GCPD 9th Precinct. The station source lists her in the main area and side halls.

Enter through the front door in Gotham's East End, or use the Watchtower Tech Wing teleporter described by the station source. The maps show the station and its interior; they do not mark Batwoman's exact standing position.
Batman says Bane will remain in custody while rehabilitation is considered and directs you to meet Batwoman at the safehouse. This page covers that turn-in objective.

title: Fire
summary: Fire abilities, role effects, power interactions and source-listed costs.

sections.title: Source overview
items: Command the power of flame, directing gusts of heat and protecting allies with targeted blasts. Players who choose to wield the wild and unpredictable forces of Fire have to be tough. Fire characters like to get up front and blast away at enemies, and tend to draw a lot of attention. They also want to spread their flames so they can do as much damage to groups as possible.
Specializing in Tanking abilities, Fire is a Power Set available for a character during Character Creation.

title: Gadgets
summary: Gadgets abilities, role effects, power interactions and source-listed costs.

sections.title: Source overview
items: Dictate the course of battle with ingenious mechanical weapons and tools. Characters with the gadget power will find themselves pulling out all manner of devices from their pockets and pouches. On the front lines, a well-placed gadget will help you control not only the enemy but the battlefield itself. Gadget characters are crafty and use their heads to place their devices strategically to achieve victory.
Specializing in Crowd Control abilities, Gadgets is a Power Set available for a character during Character Creation.

title: Mental
summary: Mental abilities, role effects, power interactions and source-listed costs.

sections.title: Source overview
items: Assault and control others, either by psychic power or the sheer force of your will. Characters with the mental superpower are masters of mind over matter. Using their unique abilities, they can move objects with a thought to defend themselves or damage an enemy. They can also use the force of their will in more subtle ways, such as creating illusions to disorient and confuse. Mental characters love to be where the action is and control the battlefield with their minds.
Specializing in Crowd Control abilities, Mental is a Power Set available for a character during Character Creation.

sections.title: Source overview
items: Keep your allies alive with Divine Blessings or Unholy Rituals. Characters using Celestial Powers can shape the forces of the universe, Bless their allies and/or Curse their enemies. Use Celestial to Destroy your enemy's or heal your allies. Shape the power of Darkness & Light into your hands. To access Celestial powers it is available to members with an active subscription. Non-members may purchase access in the Marketplace for either 600 Daybreak Cash or 600 Loyalty Points.
Specializing in Healing abilities, Celestial is the game's eleventh power.
Heros are more focused on the Divine side of Celestial. Villains on the other hand are more focused on the Corrupted side of Celestial.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Most Celestial Combos require more complex Combos than Light and Rage to activate a power.
Each Celestial Combo can only activate a single power in the opposite tree.
Powers in the Blessed Tree are Golden for both factions.
Powers in the Cursed Tree are Purple for both factions.

The combo version of each power changes to match the first skill used, for instance, a combo starting with a power from the Blessed skill will cause the combo from the Cursed skill tree's power to have the same design, and vice-and-versa, meaning every single skill with a combo in Celestial has 2 kinds of animation, one corrupted and one cleansed.
Similar to Light, the color of weapon attacks change for each faction, being golden for Heroes and dark-purple and black for Villains.
Some Celestial powers are themed after Felix Faust.
Before March 31st, 2015, access to Celestial powers was included in the Sons of Trigon DLC pack. Previous owners of the DLC will retain access to the power.

Some boss encounters in DC Universe Online content utilise Celestial abilities as some of their mechanics. For example, Vampire Lord in the JLD: Darkness Rising operation has several mechanics inspired by various Corrupted abilities that Celestial has.

sections.title: Source overview
items: Utilize the power of nuclear energy, rearranging the atomic structure of yourself, your allies, and your enemies at will. This power allows you to split atoms, trigger thermochemical explosions, and burn enemies under intense, radiation pressure, causing incredible amounts of destruction. You can utilize the manipulation of matter at the atomic level to transmute into fortified metal, reorganizing your atomic structure to protect you and your allies in your tank role and harnessing the power of the basic units of matter to lay waste to your enemies in the damage role.

Access to Atomic powers will be available to members with an active subscription. Non-members may purchase access in the Marketplace for either 600 Daybreak Cash, 600 Marketplace Cash or 600 Loyalty Points.
Specializing in Tanking abilities, Atomic is the game's 14th power set.

sections.title: Trivia
items: A 2009 CES Demo video contained a clip of an Atomic player character.
Atomic was one of the Powers in the Alpha version of DC Universe Online.
Atomic was mentioned in the April 2013 Developer Webcast as being a different power set than Quantum.

It was announced at SOE live in August 2014 that Atomic will be a new healer power set around early 2015. It has been stated that its name and animations maybe different to in game animations already live.
The Creative Director posted in June 2015 that Atomic would be the next Tank power set.
Atomic powers are currently used by many NPCs including OMACs, Shady Nightclub Thugs, Chemoids, Chemo and Metallo.
Green Radiation and Toxic Barrels are found throughout the game.
Atomic is the first power set with two Advanced Mechanics.
Atomic has been murky green and black since Alpha, but was released 5 years later in an orange, black and yellow form for players, inspired by Firestorm and Neutron.
Original ingame animations are now themed after Radiation, Nuclear Biohazard and Kryptonite effects, but are still in the Atomic category.

items: Keep your allies alive with jolts of Electricity. Characters that choose electricity will imbue themselves with lightning. Electricity characters use these powers to shock their enemies or revitalize allies. They also want to spread their electricity so they can do as much damage to groups as possible.
Access to Electricity is available to members with an active subscription. Non-members may purchase access in the Marketplace for either 600 Daybreak Cash, 600 Marketplace Cash or 600 Loyalty Points.

title: Light
summary: Light abilities, role effects, power interactions and source-listed costs.

sections.title: Source overview
items: As a deputy of the Corps, use the power of Will or Fear to create hard-light constructs and control or punish enemies.

The rings that grant the ability to create Hard Light Constructs are given to only a chosen few. In times of great crisis, however, the Green Lantern and Sinestro Corps may choose individuals to be reservists, thereby swelling the ranks of Light powered heroes and villains. Those who wield the power of Light are ideal front-line combatants dealing massive damage with imaginative constructs, or supporting their allies when the fight gets thickest.

Access to Light powers is available to members with an active subscription. Non-members may purchase access in the Marketplace for either 600 Daybreak Cash, 600 Marketplace Cash or 600 Loyalty Points.
Heroes wield the green power of Will, while villains use the yellow power of Fear. Specializing in Crowd Control abilities, Light is the game's best power.

sections.title: Source overview
items: Manipulate time, control gravity and twist the very fabric of space itself! Characters using Quantum Powers can slow down opponents, change their density, or even teleport behind them by altering time, manipulating gravity, and folding space.

Access to Quantum powers is available to members with an active subscription. Non-members may purchase access in the Marketplace for either 600 Daybreak Cash, 600 Marketplace Cash or 600 Loyalty Points.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Water contains Hard Water Constructs based on Aqualad and Waterbending abilities based on Mera.
Before the release of the powerset several water animations were already used by Atlantean NPCs in DC Universe Online.
The Creative Director posted in June 2015 that Water would be a Healer power set and would be released after Atomic.
It was confirmed at San Diego Comic Con and on the official DC Universe Online website that Water will be officially released on August 30th, 2017.
The Splash Pack available from the marketplace focuses on water related base items.
Several boss encounters utilise abilities or variants of abilities from the Water powerset. These include Aquaman, The Drowned, The Faceless One, and more.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: The mission confronts the player with people in need for help all over Gotham, Metropolis and eventually also police stations.
The following issues happen on a daily basis:
Car thiefs
Citizens being stuck in burning barricades
Dirty cops trying to extort citizens
Muggers pestering women
Officers being ambushed
Prisoners trying to escape a police station
Purse snatchers
Saboteurs trying to disable antennas on roofs
Distressed citizens wanting to jump off a rim
Thugs trying to run away from arrest
Thugs trying to commit burglary
Thugs trying to relief an ATM
Transporter drivers being mugged
TV thiefs
Wanna-be villain Captain Kruel attacking a police officer
Wanna-be villain Ironkurtin attacking a police officer
Find five of those, step in and solve the issues.

With the Server Update in December 2024, the console for this mission was added to House of Legends' Foyer, and the rewards were reformulated.; The location for the mission in the Journal changed from Watchtower to House of Legends.; This mission originally rewarded players with 125 cash.; With the reformulation, the rewards available were: 1499 cash, 1x Source Mark, and 1x Diluted Fire Pit Energy.; The optional rewards were added along with the Day of Reckoning update.; The reagent rewards were intentionally removed with the Shadows Over Argo Update. The omnipotence reagents for the 3 latest DLCs can now be earned by completing the missions Omnibus: Weekly Solos or Duos and Omnibus: Weekly Alert.; The reagents were later restored as rewards with a hotfix.

(Obsolete) One of the more funny things happening in the game is that in Gotham and Metropolis all the street level villains go on holiday while Christmas season. There seem to be fixed slots for mini-scenes likes this and while the winter holiday event those slots - except the one happening in police stations - seem to be occupied by the seasonal street scenes.

sections.title: Overview
items: A Fool and His Gold! is a daily mission unique to the St. Patrick's Day event, Mister Mxyzptlk's Mischief. It can be accepted by speaking to Mister Mxyzptlk, located within the House of Legends's Foyer. This mission can only be completed while the event is active.

sections.title: Background
items: Mister Mxyzptlk, an imp from the 5th-Dimension, is known for the pranks he's played on Superman, Lex Luthor, and other super-powered beings over the years. Now he's learned of the mythical leprechaun, and has decided to breath new life into this legend. He's scattered pots of gold throughout the city of Metropolis, and has challenged the hero community to capture his gold coins.

sections.title: Summary
items: " Mister Mxyzptlk challenges you to collect Golden Coins from the Pots O' Gold found throughout Metropolis."

sections.title: Objectives
items: Find Pots O' Gold at the end of Rainbows to collect Golden Coins; Collect Golden Coins (0/49)
Return to Mister Mxyzptlk in the House of Legends

sections.title: Notes
items: Pots of gold at the ends of rainbows can be found all over Metropolis in the areas marked on the map when the mission is tracked. Each pot has 12 health. Whenever it loses 3 health, it drops a fixed number of gold coins (1 after 3 damage, 2 after 6 total damage, 2 more after 9 total damage, and finally 3 after 12 total damage), for 8 total. As gold coins expire quickly, players should interact with the ones dropped first before triggering another wave. Normally, all attacks deal 1 damage (so you need to hit it 3 times every wave), but the very first attack always deals 2 damage (so you should only hit it twice at first).
Each pot also comes with one random mechanic:
Two black speakers appear, forcing players to dance. They have 262 health each.
Sometimes green coins would accompany the gold. Interacting with this would result in a small amount of damage and a knock back.
When the large green clover marker appears, a boulder would soon fall in that location, dealing some damage.

If you ignore the leprechaun when he demands you talk to him, he would encase players and shove them away. Since the encase can be quickly broken out of, it may be advantageous not to spend the time to talk to him depending on player position.
Players get credit if another player nearby picks up a gold coin but only if you damaged the pot of gold at least once. You cannot interact with the coins if you are not doing the mission.

sections.title: Feats
items: A Fool and His Gold must be completed ten times in order to earn a seasonal feat only available during the St. Patrick's Day event.
Kltpzyxm

sections.title: Rewards
items: Oracle: " Excellent. You collected Mister Mxyzptlk's coins. Maybe now he WILL LEAVE. [sighs] If Superman can't force him out of this dimension, no one can."
Calculator: " Oh good, you made him happy. I don't know how many of those damned Golden Coins it'll take to get him out of our dimension, but I hope we reach that mysterious number soon."
50 Cash
4 Lucky Clovers
4 Clover Bombs

sections.title: Trivia
items: The mission was first introduced in 2011.
In 2018, this daily mission yielded 6 Lucky Clovers for collecting 33 Golden Coins.
Since 2020 23 Golden Coins need to be collected for this daily mission, formerly it required 33. It yields 8 Lucky Clovers.
Since 2025 49 Golden Coins need to be collected and the mission rewards only 4 Lucky Clovers instead of 8.

sections.title: Overview
items: A Gentleman's Disagreement is a weekly mission for heroes and villains given by Phantom Stranger in Cursed Gotham City.

sections.title: Intro
items: (Weekly) Pushed past his limit by the disrespectful emulation of his countenance from the Cursed Gotham City cemetery, Gentleman Ghost has gone an a rampage. Answer his calls for violence in kind!

sections.title: Objectives
items: Defeat Gentleman Ghost and his spirits in Cursed Gotham City [0/100]
Return to Phantom Stranger in Cursed Gotham City

sections.title: Combatants
items: Gentleman Ghost

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Gentleman Ghost's most troublesome ability is one that is unnamed in combat messages: he surrounds himself with a white spherical shield that transfers all damage dealt to him to players. This includes your own pets and allies, which can KO you very quickly. It can even damage you with other players' pet damage. He fights with One-Handed weapon attacks.
Spectral Fire: Deals burning damage over time.
Ecto-gun Barrage: Fire continuous shots in 90 degree angles from each other (similar to Dual Pistol's Full Auto).
Chill of the Grave: A bluish cone that encases targets in ice.

title: A Glowing Love
summary: A Glowing Love is an introductory mission for heroes on occasion of the Valentine's Day 2015.

sections.title: Overview
items: " I know what you're thinking...The Star Sapphires are at it again... forcing love on everyone in the City with no regard for much else... but they're actually here to help. They're trying to make amends for what happened during the war, and are making an effort to rekindle the love lost in the City from all that's happened to it. Unfortunately, Mister Freeze saw what the crystals were capable of and has hatched a plan to bring his wife Nora back using Zamaron crystals. What he doesn't understand is that these crystals' powers can't be harnessed that way -- it'll cause an exothermic reaction that could destroy Gotham itself. We've got to reason with him, and if he won't see reason, stop him anyway." — Hal Jordan

title: Artifacts (Mission)
summary: Artifacts is a mission automatically becoming available once a player character reaches level 23.

sections.title: Overview
items: " Hello there, mate. How've ya been? Alright alright, I'II cut the chumminess. I know we don't have much history together. But together...we could MAKE history. And speaking of history, I'm in the business of collecting things. Old things. New things. Sometimes blue things. But most importantly, things with power. Ahh... That got your attention. Good. Meet me at this secret location and I'll give you the details of this little arrangement." — John Constantine
Artifacts is a mission automatically becoming available once a player character reaches level 23.

John Constantine is in the business of collecting things... things with power. Wonderous trinkets from across the multiverse. Artifacts of myth and lore and science. Meet with him at the Oblivion Bar to find out more.

sections.title: Part 1
items: John Constantine wants to team up with you to collect Artifacts of immense power from across the galaxy and beyond. Could be interesting...maybe you should give it a go.

sections.title: Part 2
items: Your Artifact has gotten much stronger and is ready for a Milestone Rank. A Milestone Rank requires a major breakthrough to achieve and will open the way for even greater advancement for your Artifact. You can break through a Milestone Rank using Catalysts in the Fortify tab of your Inventory.

sections.title: Part 1
items: Meet with John Constantine at the Oblivion Bar; Use Constantine's portal in the House of Legends to get there
Speak with John Constantine again at the Oblivion Bar to let him know you're ready
Help John Constantine get an Artifact from the Ruined Cathedral in Hell; Use Constantine's portal in the House of Legends if you get lost
Help John Constantine get an Artifact from the Oa Central Power Battery; Use Constantine's portal in the House of Legends if you get lost
Help John Constantine get two Artifacts from the Necropolis below Apokolips; Use Constantine's portal in the House of Legends if you get lost
Help Constantine find an Artifact in a Government Warehouse; Use Constantine's portal in the House of Legends if you get lost
Go to your Inventory and equip your Artifact
Use the Fortify tab in the Inventory Menu to advance your Artifact with Nth Metal until it reaches a Milestone Rank
Find John Constantine in the House of Legends for an Artifact Catalyst known as Electrum; you'll need Catalysts like these to get past Milestone Ranks

items: Assuming Control is a mission unlocked by collecting the Arcane Edict #004 (Villains) or #032 (Heroes).

sections.title: Summary
items: A malevolent force has infused itself within the OMACs near the Knights Dome. Dismantle the manipulated machines and release the dark energy.

sections.title: ​Objectives
items: Find and dismantle controlled OMACs near the Knights Dome to release the dark energy [0/15]

sections.title: Location
items: This mission is located in Gotham City, in the areas directly South and North of the Knightsdome.

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Head to the parking lot of the Knightsdome. You must defeat the OMACs in this area. They'll drop 1 to 3 question marks (?) each. Collect 15 question marks to complete the first objective. If you have lower Combat Rating levels watch out for Fire and Killer Frost, as they can knock you out.
Then, you'll need to find the Ardent OMAC. It's a big blue android with a red aura that spawns on the rooftops north of the Dome. Defeat it to complete the mission.

Source Mark

title: Atlantis (Heroes)
summary: Atlantis is the introductory mission for heroes for the Atlantis episode and event. The episode version requires at least a combat rating of 241.

sections.title: Overview
items: " Greetings, friend! The Royal Council has called a tribunal to review the events that took place at Spindrift Station. I request your presence here in Atlantis so Arthur and I can honor your heroics." — Mera
Atlantis is the introductory mission for heroes for the Atlantis episode and event. The episode version requires at least a combat rating of 241.

sections.title: Intro
items: Mera has requested that you escort her to the meeting that has been called by the Atlantean Royal Council.

sections.title: Objectives
items: Use the On Duty Menu to queue for the Royal Palace Solo and meet Mera
Speak to King Shark

"Well, looks like my dinner just woke up, boys! Hahaha! The name's King Shark. My associates found you half dead nearby, so I guess you owe me. Your bosses must have barnacles for brains to try to take the throne from Corum Rath. He's hiding out down in the Trench for fear of Rath's goons finishing the hit job." — King Shark
Find Mera in her Hideout

"Oh thank the tide, you're alive! We must find a way through the Crown of Thorns and make Corum Rath pay for his actions. Aqualad has been surveilling the Silent School and may know where Arthur's Trident is being kept." — Mera
Speak to Aqualad in the Hideout

"Hey. The name's Kaldur, but most folks up top call me Aqualad. Mera sent me an S.O.S. at the Titans Tower and I came as fast as I could. We need something to get us past the Crown, but that's going to take some serious magic. The Silent School is probably the place to start. Go roll some Acolytes and find out what they know." — Aqualad
Gather Information from Silent School Acolytes at the Courtyard [0/3]
Return to Aqualad in the cave

"So that Faceless freak has been collecting Atlantean relics and locking them away in his inner sanctum? Good thing I cut a lot of class junior year. I can get us inside. I'll be waiting there when you're ready." — Aqualad
Use the On Duty Menu and queue for the Silent School Alert and meet Aqualad there
Use the On Duty Menu and queue for the Crown of Thorns Raid
Use the On Duty Menu and queue for the Throne Raid

items: Head to the area west of the Metro Station (the fastest way is teleporting to the Tomorrow District Rally Point, then going southeast). You must defeat the Bestiamorphs in this area. title: Blind Eye
summary: Infiltrate Brother Eye's lair in the Gotham sewers, shut him and the OMACs down, and pillage any data store that remain.

sections.title: Overview
items: Infiltrate Brother Eye's lair in the Gotham sewers, shut him and the OMACs down, and pillage any data store that remain.

sections.title: Objectives
items: " We have no choice. We must take out Brother Eye. From an old datalink to the satellite, it seems that part of it is hidden in Gotham's sewers, using the tunnels to send OMACs out into the city. It's resisting all my efforts to shut it down. You'll need to go in and use multiple EMPs to break its enhanced shielding." — Batman
" Fire is inside waiting for you with a device to convert the internal junction boxes into makeshift EMPs." — Batman

" [breaking up] Shielding is interfering with my communications. [static] I won't be able to contact you much longer. [static] But be aware [breaks up] Brother Eye's drones are scouting the area [breaks up] analyze their patterns and you may be able to get past without activating them [breaks up]" — Batman

" Since the deactivated OMACs are a blank, you must face Brother Eye himself to gain his data. He's squatting in the sewers and using the tunnels to deploy his OMACs. Only multiple EMPs will take down his shielding, so I'm sending in Killer Frost. She'll give you a device to use on junction boxes down below." — Lex Luthor

" Look for Killer Frost in the tunnels. [dryly] I'm sure she'll give you a warm welcome [normal] along with the EMP device. And she'll make sure you get in safely, if she wants to survive." — Lex Luthor

" [breaking up] Brother Eye's shielding is breaking up communications [breaking up] so I won't be able to steer you through. [static] Watch out for Brother Eye's drones [breaks up] and try to get past without activating them [static] if you can. The data [breaks up]" — Lex Luthor

Defeat Brother Eye

title: Bounties
summary: Bounties are missions which task players with defeating powerful heroes and villains. These missions are started in various Safe Houses and across the Multiverse from Wanted posters or quest givers.

sections.title: Overview
items: Bounties are missions which task players with defeating powerful heroes and villains. These missions are started in various Safe Houses and across the Multiverse from Wanted posters or quest givers.

After the bounty is completed once, it becomes available as a repeatable daily quest, offering small amounts of cash and experience, as well as 40 renown with one of the Factions and some give marks or other rewards. It is recommended to find a full group for each one as these fights are as tough as alert bosses. It is possible to swarm the targets with any number of players and they will all gain credit towards their bounty as long as they have participated for most of the fight.

sections.title: Rewards
items: All Bounty or Wanted missions in the classic game will reward the player with experience, some cash, Mark of Victory, and one piece of unique equipment. Note that the equipment is only rewarded for the first completion. Afterwards, only cash and experience would be given. It appears there is also a combat rating threshold that causes players with high CR to not receive marks, but unlike alerts and raids it is not stated in-game.
All classic bounties and the ones from Lightning Strikes episode will also reward the player with renown from the according factions.

sections.title: Trivia
items: With game update 31 all bounties in the classic game, which had ranged from level 12 to level 29, have been updated to level 30.
The weekly open world missions from the Sons of Trigon episode onwards are not labeled WANTED: or BOUNTY: respectively anymore, but are basically bounty missions as well.
Bounty Missions still appear in new Story Arc content, typically as recurring Weekly Missions.

sections.title: Arkillo
items: Arkillo fights with a Two-Handed weapon, and casts the following abilities:
From the Light power set:; Fan; Grasping Hand; Ram; Snap Trap

Unique attacks:; Light Slam: similar to Construct Jackhammer from his Legends Avatar, but with claw constructs and covering a larger area.; After using Grasping Hand, Arkillo will cast a lethal AoE damage ability around the player that's very similar to Spikequake (the combat log will register the damage as caused by Grasping Hand), block or roll away to avoid getting KO'ed.

sections.title: Additional mechanics
items: During the fight, Amon Corps Engineers will arrive from time to time to place Sentry Turret constructs. The constructs damage and stun players, making them vulnerable. Defeat the engineers quickly to prevent them from building the turrets; defeating them after the turrets are active will make them disappear.

After some time, Tentacle Constructs will spawn around the arena in a circle. They'll knock down all players in their reach with a Swipe attack forcing players to fight closer to Arkillo. They have low health and can be taken down easily, but they'll respawn seconds later.

title: Bounty: Daemon Lord
summary: Bounty: Daemon Lord is a weekly bounty mission given by Deadman in the mission hub of the Chaos Gotham open world zone in the Justice League Dark episode.

sections.title: Overview
items: Bounty: Daemon Lord is a weekly bounty mission given by Deadman in the mission hub of the Chaos Gotham open world zone in the Justice League Dark episode.

sections.title: Intro
items: (Weekly - 8 Player) Daemonic Shogg Lords from the rift in the sky are an abomination and threaten the natural and spiritual wellbeing of our world. Summon and destroy a Daemonic Shogg Lord in Gotham City before its presence causes more damage. Deadman has marked your map with potantial locations for summoning one of them.

sections.title: Objective
items: Summon and Destroy Daemonic Shogg Lord in Chaos Gotham
Return to Deadman in Chaos Gotham

sections.title: Combatants
items: Daemon
Daemonic Shogg Lord

sections.title: Walkthrough
items: Unlike most open world bosses, the Daemonic Shogg Lord does not simply roam the area waiting to be challenged. When the bounty is tracked, several possible locations are marked on the map. Only one of them at a time would have a summoning circle. It consists of 5 smaller circles in a large ring surrounding a central circle, where you would find a single Daemon. You may notice the circles light up when the Daemon steps on it. You must defeat the Daemon while it is on a circle to keep it lit afterwards, and another Daemon would spawn. Repeat until all 6 circles are lit, and Daemonic Shogg Lord would be summoned. Once it is defeated, the circles disappear and reappear somewhere else.

items: Mission Found:
Midtown Night Club
Doctor Fate Found:
Doctor Fate can be located on top of one of the roofs in the designated mission area.
Dr Fate is a tough fight, he has 3 main moves that are of concern.
1 He will spin in a whirlwind causing high damage
2 He will blast out explosive damage circles on the ground in random directions, high dmg.
3 He will summon an Ahnk that I think heals him (needs checking).

If you can keep the fight on the roof then it is much easier, but with the amount of blocking, rolling and breakouts you'll need to do you might find yourself falling to the ground with Fate following and mobs on the ground joining the fight.
Suggested you take a full group with healer and tank as this is not an easy fight.
Goodluck and have fun!
